description: The release-level product qualification: the composed product installed into clean disposable repositories from PACKED ARTIFACTS ONLY, driving scoped intake through the full checkpoint path to merge-ready under two distinct repository policies. Every claim below names the leg that proved it. The packed leg is re-executable — `npm run qualify:product` reproduces it end to end — the fixture leg names in-process sensors that exist and run on every CI leg, and the authenticated-host leg records an operator-owned native Claude result flowing through the same packed path. Claims that no leg establishes are listed under notProvenHere rather than implied by silence.

criteria.statement: the product that delivered the work was loaded from an installed, digest-addressed generation root, never from the source checkout
criteria.evidence: the five workspace packages were npm-packed and installed into an isolated tree outside the repository; that tree's installer packed and installed a composition generation; and the kernel that drove both deliveries was imported from inside the read-only generation root. The loaded entry is an inventory member of the installed composition manifest and its bytes re-hash to the manifest's recorded sha256, so the claim binds to the digest rather than to the driver's intent.

criteria.statement: an already-scoped contract reaches merge-ready through plan, implement, trusted sensor, two-lens review, compound, admission, neutral tracked record, and finish line
criteria.evidence: both disposable repositories completed the frozen checkpoint path and reported state `completed`, with a non-empty discharged-obligation set and an operator-intervention counter of zero. Each policy lens ran as a distinct native invocation under an installation-owned capability outside the admitted filesystem grant; the installed Claude adapter preserved the exact raw envelope bytes and required the exact bound persona, contract, sensor evidence, and review-instruction bytes to be the prompt context the host submitted. One atomic journal append per result fed the sole manifest builder, admission gate, tracked-record verifier, and finish line.

criteria.statement: each completed native-provider reviewer result is capability-bound to exact provider/session/workspace/fence/trust/candidate/persona/prompt context and reaches the existing evidence gate without sidecar authority or a second manifest path
criteria.evidence: for both repositories the trusted operator-owned driver created a distinct review snapshot outside the model/reviewer writable roots, and the packed product only validated and bound it before preparing one handoff per policy reviewer. The snapshot is reviewer-read-only through the admitted host grant; the operator-owned same-user host is trusted and retains lifecycle authority. The product required installation-owned root and invocation proofs, bound and rechecked the current trust-revocation epoch immediately before attempt acceptance, adapted exact Claude-native envelopes, applied shared review-green coherence, and accepted normalized results only through original-revision CAS. Attempts/replay are journal-derived with no sidecar authority before the existing recorder and single manifest builder. Source sensors falsify forged proofs; wrong workspace, fence, session, provider, trust epoch, candidate snapshot, persona, or submitted context; partial, failed, moved, approved-but-blocking, and conflicting results; missing or tampered accepted bytes; mixed provider-run triples; concurrent callbacks; fresh attempt ids under suspended tuples; concurrent exact-tuple conflict-marker durability; and changes-requested approval.

criteria.statement: an authenticated Claude Code review reaches merge-ready from its retained raw native result through shared ingestion, the existing attempt journal and sole manifest builder, admission, and tracked-record verification
criteria.evidence: Claude Code 2.1.252 reviewed both exact candidates through four native UUID child sessions: one outcome-correctness and one testing-policy invocation per repository, sharing exactly one provider run and final pass inside each delivery. Every untouched outer envelope and SHA-256 is retained; every accepted normalized result carries its raw bytes/digest, exact consumed persona+contract+sensor+instruction prompt digest, session/run, workspace, fence, and candidate. Installation-owned root/invocation bindings are retained outside the admitted filesystem grant. Each delivery journal contains exactly two attempt.artifact.recorded entries and one evidence.reference.recorded entry; the sole manifest contains both provider-result and reviewer-approval artifacts with the common run provenance; tracked records verified; and each journal reached one completed transition. Earlier live refusals remain retained and accepted nothing. The operator-owned driver launched the native sessions; the product only decided and recorded evidence.

criteria.statement: an outcome-only work request is scoped iteratively by a product-owned turn and reaches merge-ready through the same single operator confirmation
criteria.evidence: disposable-beta hands over a work request carrying no contract; the lane runs openIntake under the read-only intake grant, one clarification exchange, a retained draft, and presentDraft — converging on the SAME binding-owned confirmation channel the already-scoped lane uses, and then through the identical checkpoint path to merge-ready. disposable-alpha takes the already-scoped lane, so both intake entries are exercised from packed artifacts rather than one being deferred to a source-importing sensor.

criteria.statement: both deliveries complete with no tracker and no control plane configured
criteria.evidence: no tracker and no control plane exist anywhere in this installation — the composition pin's control-plane contract version is the reserved placeholder — and the compiled disposable policy's tracker-absence fallback is proceed-without-tracker. Both deliveries reached `completed` with a non-empty discharged-obligation set and zero operator interventions, so trackerless and control-plane-free completeness is what the lane actually ran rather than a separate probe. Stated as the honest shape it is: these are properties of every run here, not an isolated scenario.

criteria.statement: a second repository changes policy without forking workflows or harness semantics
criteria.evidence: disposable-alpha and disposable-beta differ in gate id, identity token, review-neutral set, record-neutral set, delivery-record location, source layout, test classification, contracted outcome, and intake lane — beta declares a consumer-owned `beta-tree/v1` token because `deliverable-tree/v1` pins its own narration set. What differs is the tracked GATE CONFIGURATION, which is what an adopter controls at this layer; the product's compiled repository policy for a disposable repository is a fixed document parameterized by repository id and charter digests, and the record does not claim otherwise. Both repositories were served by ONE installed generation — the same installation path and active pointer, observed once and reused — and each tracked record landed in its own policy-declared neutral tree, so the record location came from policy rather than from a product-wide constant.

criteria.statement: the product launches no coding-agent runtime and owns no workspace lifecycle
criteria.evidence: every normalized command the product ran through its INJECTED EXEC PORT during both deliveries was inventoried per repository, and each lane's inventory is non-empty. The observed executable inventory is `git` and `node`; the detector resolves Git global options before deciding the subcommand and recognizes exact coding-agent file targets passed through Node. The trusted host created and retired every delivery worktree and reviewer-read-only review snapshot outside model/reviewer writable roots; the product only validated and bound them. This criterion is exactly a port-routed normalized-command observation plus the facade's static non-orchestration contract, not an exhaustive process-table claim. See knownLimitations for launch shapes and direct subprocess modules outside that observation.

criteria.statement: the qualification fixture profile is use-time bound in both temporal directions
criteria.evidence: a fixture manifest refuses to activate without the operator-supplied qualification flag (`qualification_flag_required`); the same flag is refused on a production manifest (`qualification_flag_refused`); and a flagged installation refuses to register a delivery in a repository its receipt does not list (`disposable_repository_refused`) while both listed repositories completed through that same installation

criteria.statement: two contract-changing updates leave every superseded generation retained and resumable, and rollback reaches a retained non-revoked target
criteria.evidence: sequences 2 and 3 were packed and activated through the maintenance lane; all three generations remained in the installation inventory; the original pinned generation still loaded through `loadPinnedGeneration`, which is the resume path's precondition; and an offline pointer rollback to the retained middle generation succeeded

criteria.statement: revoking a pinned generation fences live work into security_blocked, and a revoked generation is not a rollback target
criteria.evidence: a delivery registered successfully against the generation (the control half), the generation was then revoked through the maintenance lane, the next mutation-capable operation was refused, and the delivery's state read `security_blocked` — a refusal without the fenced state would leave it resumable. Rollback to that same revoked generation was refused with `generation_revoked`.

criteria.statement: the closure verifier is invocable from an installed package, and the emitted hook command resolves against a real staged path in an installed generation
criteria.evidence: Both halves are proven from a tarball install outside the repository, never from a source import — which is the whole point, since a source-importing suite cannot see either defect by construction. The verifier is reached through the package's `exports` map (resolved, not path-joined) and CALLED against the generation the installer just installed, which a name check alone would not establish. The hook command is read back off the composed settings file the host actually reads, decided against the composition manifest's staged inventory — launcher, containment, and staging membership, so neither the command string nor the staged path can carry the claim alone — and then executed against the installed generation, where it produces the interceptor's own deny for an unattested session. The negative is proven too: a copy of the generation with the staged entry removed is refused by the published verifier with `closure_digest_mismatch`, and a separate installation, corrupted after install, refuses to bind a workspace at all — the delivery's pinned-generation trust check, which is where a root missing a staged file is caught before any command is composed. Both refusals carry a control: the two deliveries bound sessions against the intact generation, and the corrupted installation registered its delivery successfully while the entry was still there.

criteria.statement: every claimed sensor is mutated red, and a comment-only no-op is not
criteria.evidence: the lane's judgements are pure functions falsified in both directions by scripts/qualify-product.test.ts, its COMPOSITION is falsified (dropping either half of the observation verdict is caught directly, because the wiring test's degenerate input can only ever witness the vacuity half), and its WIRING is falsified too — the lane is driven for real on an input that cannot get past its first step and required to return the vacuity findings rather than an empty list. The pre-existing rules' mutations each produced a named failing test — deliberately enumerated rather than counted, because the numeral is the part nobody checks: the agent-runtime rule never reporting AND always reporting; policy-independence never firing; anti-vacuity dropping its enumeration; the two repositories converging; path containment becoming a prefix test; the refusal detector ignoring an allowed result; the per-lane inventory collapsing into one shared counter; the second intake lane disappearing; either half of the observation verdict dropped; and the exit ceasing to call it. The process sensor additionally falsifies Git workspace lifecycle hidden behind global options and an agent launcher hidden behind Node. ELEVEN FURTHER mutations on the packed-surface rules, likewise each naming a failing test: the resolved-name enumeration ceasing to report emptiness; the membership loop never reporting; the required-name set emptied; the launcher check dropped; the staging check weakened to a path-only sensor AND to a command-string-only sensor — the pair an incomplete sensor passes, since a check on the command string alone survives an absent path and a check on the staged path alone survives a command pointing elsewhere; containment dropped; the empty-command, empty-inventory and no-path-member guards dropped; and the command-line parser degraded to a whitespace split. Weakening the shared path-containment helper to a prefix comparison is counted ONCE, above: it is the same one-line edit, and it now reddens a named test in both families rather than surviving in this one. FOUR PRODUCT mutations were falsified against the packed lane itself rather than against a pure rule, because the two defects this candidate closes live in the product: removing the verifier's re-export, restoring the tsx launcher, staging the entry while pointing the command elsewhere, and emitting the entry's unresolved spelling each turned the lane red with a named finding, the last one only because the lane EXECUTES the emitted command rather than reading it. A comment-only edit left all 58 green — 49 in the lane's own suite and 9 in the record checker, counted rather than apportioned — and a comment-only edit in the facade left the packed lane clean.

packedLeg.statement: the composed product installed from packed artifacts into clean disposable repositories and driven to merge-ready. Re-executable: `npm run qualify:product`.
packedLeg.sourceAccess: the driver imports nothing from packages/. It reaches the product twice, both times through an artifact: the npm-packed tarball install tree supplies the operator-facing installer — resolved through the package's own `exports` map rather than by joining a path into its src/, so what the lane drives is the published surface and not merely the shipped layout — and the installed generation root supplies the product that drives the deliveries.
packedLeg.crossPlatform: the same lane runs as a release-workflow step on ubuntu-latest, and that run is the cross-platform evidence this gate requires. PENDING FOR THIS RECORD: the Linux leg for this candidate had not reported when these observations were written, so the digest above is the macOS one only and no second platform is claimed here. Nothing in the lane compares the two digests; the comparison is the operator's, and this field is where it lands.
packedLeg.hostLane: in-process. The driver stands in for the host task the way the walking skeleton's scenario sensor does: it creates the worktrees and submits the typed stage results a host would. The product launches nothing either way, which is what the process inventory above records.
packedLeg.hostVersionCurrency: The ordinary packed lane and the authenticated acceptance both carry Claude Code 2.1.252 into their reviewer results and manifests. The strict filesystem admission floor is reverified at that version. The older Tier 2 lifecycle and descendant-teardown observations were not re-driven and do not silently gain a current-version claim; same-workspace resume remains closed.

authenticatedHostAcceptance.statement: operator-owned Claude Code reviews over the packed generation ran one native invocation per policy reviewer and reached completed delivery through capability-checked ingestion, journal-authoritative attempts, the sole manifest builder, admission, tracked-record verification, and finish line

packedSurfaceFindings.observation: the installer's internal generation-closure verifier was not reachable through the package's single `exports` entry, so an adopter installing the published package could not invoke the verification the installer exists to offer
packedSurfaceFindings.consequence: `verifyGenerationClosure` is re-exported from the kernel's one published entry — the `exports` map itself is unchanged, since widening it was never what the verifier needed — and the packed leg now CALLS it through that entry against the generation it was just handed, so the claim is an invocation rather than a name check

packedSurfaceFindings.observation: the facade's model-external hook command named a `tsx` binary under a `node_modules` directory the packed composition never stages, so the command an installed generation emitted pointed at nothing
packedSurfaceFindings.consequence: the command now runs on the running Node executable — this repository ships zero runtime dependencies and the emitted command holds to that too — and names the hook entry the composition actually stages, resolved through the filesystem so the entry recognizes the spelling as its own. The packed leg decides the vector against the composition manifest's staged set and then EXECUTES it against the installed generation, requiring the interceptor's own deny for an unattested session

packedSurfaceFindings.observation: a hook command naming an unresolved spelling of the staged entry — the default spelling of the temp root on some platforms, reached through a symlink — started the process and then ran nothing, because the entry recognizes direct invocation by comparing its argument vector against its symlink-resolved module URL
packedSurfaceFindings.consequence: found by executing the emitted command rather than by reading it: the vector passed every staging assertion and produced empty output. The facade now emits the resolved spelling, and the packed leg requires the interceptor's deny on stdout rather than a clean exit, which is what distinguishes an interceptor that ran from one that silently did not

fixtureLeg.statement: properties the packed leg does not itself exercise, proven in-process by sensors that run on every CI leg. Named here so the record's coverage is checkable, never copied. NOT a claim that the packed leg could not reach them: most are ordinary exported facade surfaces and the packed leg simply does not drive them — the honest reason is scope, not unreachability.

sensors.property: the lane's own rules hold in both directions, and the required probe and lifecycle sets are non-empty and enumerated
planted implementation, sensor-rewrite, and reviewer failures loop through remediation; interruption and fresh-task takeover replay no accepted work; model-minted confirmations are refused

revocation before resume and during active work, explicit compatible migration, re-preparation and evidence invalidation, profile-mismatched rebinding refusal, and installation identity mismatch fencing

the binding attests grant, workspace, fence, and projection before any tool is visible; stale and sibling attestations open nothing; the product never launches Claude Code and manages no host agents or workspaces
outcome-only iterative scoping and tracker-absent completeness
sensor contradiction and evidence admission through the existing harness boundary
Claude and Codex-shaped native results share one closed host-neutral handoff/result contract and only Claude supplies a native-envelope adapter
host interruption and fresh-task resume across checkpoints
each tarball installs alone outside the workspace and its entry point imports and runs

notProvenHere: A live authenticated provider-result lane on any host other than Claude Code. The Codex-shaped fixture proves the shared contract only; it is not a native Codex result and is not counted as one.

A Codex delivery lane, of any kind. Codex CAPABILITIES are graded in qualifications/host-admission-capabilities.json (codex-cli, Tier 1 mutation floor live-probed model-free; Tier 2 lifecycle and Tier 3 descendant teardown provisional), so the Codex surface is not unknown. What does not exist in this repository is a Codex host-binding module or a qualified Codex delivery integration to drive a lane with — that is V26-1478, which this ticket lists as a blocker and which is still open. The second-host half of the release claim therefore belongs to V26-1478 and was deliberately not attempted here; the ticket's own carve-out (a sub-Tier-1 second host runs as capability verification only) does not create a delivery lane where no binding exists.

Advancing the shipped reviewer persona set alone through the agent-skills corpus validation and release build. That advance happens in the agent-skills repository, and its effect here is the three re-stamped composition digest constants — inherent to a digest-pinned composition, not per-persona coupling.
Replacing one host integration alone, and the planted duplicated-workflow coupling that must fail. Both need a second host integration to replace or duplicate against.

A control-plane-absent lane as a distinct scenario. No control plane is configured anywhere in this repository, so every lane above already runs without one; that is an absence rather than a probe, and it is recorded as such rather than claimed as coverage.
Native subagent delegation inside a qualified session. The product neither supervises nor observes it by design; what the packed leg proves is that no agent process was launched at all.

The production interactive confirmation channel and the OS-native assertion source. The packed leg runs the confirmation-fixture profile and the qualification-fixture assertion source, which the installer production-rejects — that rejection is itself one of the probes above.

Windows packing and installation. The packed leg ran on the macOS platform recorded above; the Linux leg's status for this candidate is stated in crossPlatform rather than asserted here. No claim is made about Windows.
knownLimitations: The two disposable repositories are driven by one process in sequence, so the lane proves that one release serves two policies and not that two installations serve them concurrently.

The no-agent-process evidence is exactly a normalized-command observation on the injected exec port, not a process-table sweep. It covers direct forbidden executable basenames, Git workspace subcommands after global options such as `-C`/`-c`/`--git-dir`, and exact coding-agent file targets launched through Node. Shell command strings (`sh -c`), environment launchers, Node eval/loader forms such as `node -e`, and dynamically constructed targets are outside this detector's claim. Candidate.ts, records.ts, substrate/assertion-source.ts and substrate/preflight.ts import node:child_process directly, so launches there are also outside the port inventory. The facade retains a separate static non-orchestration contract; this qualification does not inflate that contract into exhaustive runtime tracing.

Each disposable repository's tracked harness.config.ts resolves defineHarnessConfig from the npm-tarball tree rather than the generation root, so the config object crossing into the generation-root facade is minted by a second kernel module instance. That is the adopter's real shape — an adopter installs the package and imports it from node_modules — but it means the config-construction half of the product is exercised only through the tarball.

The product half of 'packed artifacts only' is a composition generation packed from the source checkout and imported by a checkout-shaped path inside the generation root. The kernel's npm `exports` map and `files` list are therefore exercised for the INSTALLER half but not for the product half; `sensor:standalone` is what covers those for every package, and this lane does not duplicate it.

Several judgements inside the heavy lane are not extracted and so are not falsifiable by the fast suite: the three-generations-distinct check in the lifecycle step, the internals of the outcome-only scoping turn, and the emitted-hook-command wrapper — reading the composed settings file, slicing the host's appended arguments off the vector, executing it, and the bind probe's control half. The RULE the wrapper feeds is extracted and falsified in both directions; its wiring is not. All of them are reachable only from a full `npm run qualify:product` run, which is the pre-existing posture for everything inside driveRepository; the checked-in record — zero findings, with beta recorded under intakeMode outcome-only and seven negative probes satisfied — is the evidence that they ran. Deliberately not counted: a numeral here is the part nobody checks.

The packed leg proves the emitted hook command runs the staged interceptor and denies an unattested session. The separate authenticated lane proves Claude emitted the retained review envelopes under the strict composed sandbox, while the one-off sandbox characterization proves OS containment. Neither makes host launch or hook driving a product responsibility.

The packed provider-result leg uses a structurally native Claude result envelope written by the qualification fixture, not an authenticated Claude session. It proves packed reachability and the full handoff-to-ingestion-to-gate wiring; the explicit operator lane separately establishes that Claude itself emitted the retained envelopes.

The facade's own `hook_entry_missing` refusal is unexercised. Every guarded operation reloads the delivery's pinned generation and re-verifies its digest closure, so a generation missing the staged hook entry is already refused as `trust_ineligible` — which is what the bind probe pins, because it is what fires. The hook-entry branch keeps the resolution total for a race after that verification, and no sensor here reaches it.
